rules.sentence: Neurologic involvement in EGPA often presents as mononeuritis multiplex or mixed sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy, with wrist or foot drop being a common symptom.
Peripheral neuropathy is seen in 75% to 80% of cases.
Additionally, 10% to 39% of neurological manifestations may involve central nervous system vasculitis, leading to cerebral infarctions or hemorrhages.[46]
Cranial nerve palsies are uncommon in EGPA; however, involvement of cranial nerves II, III, VI, and VIII has been reported.
Ischemic optic neuritis is the most frequently reported cranial neuropathy.
Autonomic neuropathies may contribute to cardiac dysrhythmias observed in EGPA patients.[47]
While central nervous system vasculitis can lead to significant neurological symptoms, most other neurological manifestations typically respond well to standard therapy.
